hints: The answer is the longest run of equal bits.
Flipping one bit affects only the two boundaries next to it.
Maintain run boundaries in an ordered set and run lengths in a multiset.
analogy: A flipped bit splits or joins only neighboring strips of equal color.
example: For 0011, flipping the second bit gives 0111, whose longest run is 3.
algorithm: Keep ordered boundaries at positions where adjacent bits differ, plus sentinels at 0 and n. Keep all distances between consecutive boundaries in a multiset. When flipping position i, toggle each valid boundary between i-1 and i and between i and i+1. Inserting a boundary replaces one run length by two; deleting it replaces two lengths by their sum. After both updates, output the largest multiset value.
correctness: A boundary exists exactly where consecutive bits differ, so consecutive boundaries delimit precisely the maximal equal-bit runs. A flip changes equality only on its two incident boundaries. Updating the corresponding lengths preserves the invariant, and the largest stored length is the requested answer.
complexity: For string length n and q flips, time is O((n+q) log n) and space O(n).
